                 f"{R.values['cve_chart_first']['text']} to {R.values['cve_last']['text']}.\n"
                 "Credit = the CNA credits field only, matched to named AI systems. Method credit: Epoch AI (CC BY).",
                 color=INK2, fontsize=7)
        fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.08, right=0.98, top=0.88, bottom=0.12)
        self.save_fig(fig, "cve-ai-credit.svg")

    # ------------------------------------------------------------ deck
    def render(self, head: str) -> None:
        tpl = TEMPLATE.read_text()
        fm_end = tpl.index("\n---\n", 4) + 5
        first = tpl[:fm_end].count("\n") + 1
        for i, line in enumerate(tpl[fm_end:].splitlines(), first):
            bare = re.sub(r"\{\{\w+\}\}", "", re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", "", line))
            bare = re.sub(r"!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)", "", bare)   # image directives (w:900) are layout, not data
            bad = sorted(tokens(bare) - STATIC_TOKENS)
            if bad:
                self.errs.append(f"deck.template.md:{i}: hand-typed numerals {bad}")
            for q in re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", line)):
                if not re.fullmatch(r"\{\{q_\w+\}\}", q):
                    self.errs.append(f"deck.template.md:{i}: quoted text must be one quote binding: \"{q}\"")
        self.reg.put("generated_notice", f"<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build_edition.py --codebook {self.codebook} from {head}. "
                     "Edit deck/deck.template.md, not this file. -->", source="build", how="notice")
        vals = {k: v["text"] for k, v in self.reg.values.items()}
        missing = sorted(set(re.findall(r"\{\{(\w+)\}\}", tpl)) - set(vals))
        self.errs += [f"unresolved binding {{{{{m}}}}}" for m in missing]
        md = re.sub(r"\{\{(\w+)\}\}", lambda m: vals.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)), tpl)
        out_body = re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", "", md[md.index("\n---\n", 4) + 5:], flags=re.S)
        out_body = re.sub(r"!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)", "", out_body)
        self.check_text("DECK.md", out_body)
        self.outs["DECK.md"] = md.encode()

    def run(self) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], list[str]]:
        display.selftest()
        if not self.preflight():
            return {}, self.errs
        head = git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
        OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        self.register_static(head)
        self.earnings()
        self.questions()
        self.dialogue()
        self.cve()
        self.render(head)
        stamp = {
            "edition_of": head,
            "codebook": {"risk": self.codebook, "risk_file": self.cb["file"], "risk_blake3": b3(ROOT / self.cb["file"]),
                         "question_intents": QUESTIONS["file"]},
            "rule": f"positive = DeBERTa and ModernBERT both >= {self.reg.values['threshold']['text']}",
            "rounding": "half up from the exact fraction of integer counts (scripts/display.py)",
            "dag_lock_blake3": b3(ROOT / "dag.lock.tsv"),
            "paper_v0": f"{PAPER}@{PAPER_V0}",
            "tools": {"python": "duckdb==2.0.0 matplotlib==3.10.7 blake3==1.0.11",
                      "render": "npx @marp-team/marp-cli@4.1.2 DECK.md --pptx --allow-local-files"},
            "values": {k: v for k, v in sorted(self.reg.values.items()) if k != "generated_notice"},
            "inputs": {p: b3(ROOT / p) for p in sorted(self.inputs()) if (ROOT / p).is_file()},
            "outputs": {k: blake3.blake3(v).hexdigest() for k, v in sorted(self.outs.items())},
        }
        self.outs["deck/STAMP.json"] = (json.dumps(stamp, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n").encode()
        return self.outs, self.errs


OUTPUTS = ["DECK.md", "deck/STAMP.json", "deck/ai-risk-by-year.svg", "deck/risk-ranking-ttm.svg",
           "deck/intent-ttm.svg", "deck/dialogue-space.svg", "deck/cve-ai-credit.svg"]


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("--codebook", required=True, choices=sorted(CODEBOOKS))
    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="rebuild and compare; leave the tree unchanged")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    before = {p: (ROOT / p).read_bytes() for p in OUTPUTS if (ROOT / p).exists()}

    def restore() -> None:
        for p in OUTPUTS:
            if p in before:
                (ROOT / p).write_bytes(before[p])
            elif (ROOT / p).exists():
                (ROOT / p).unlink()
    outs, errs = Build(a.codebook).run()
    if errs:
        restore()
        print("build failed:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errs), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if a.check:
        diff = sorted(p for p in OUTPUTS if before.get(p) != outs.get(p))
        restore()
        print("edition is current" if not diff else "edition would change: " + ", ".join(diff))
        return 1 if diff else 0
    for p, v in outs.items():
        (ROOT / p).write_bytes(v)
    print(f"built edition of {json.loads(outs['deck/STAMP.json'])['edition_of'][:12]} with risk codebook "
          f"{a.codebook}. Review `git diff`, then commit.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

4	  - Inputs are exact: int counts or fractions.Fraction. A float raises
5	    TypeError, because a float has already been rounded once (binary) and
6	    often twice (a rounded table column). Percentages are computed from counts.
7	  - One rounding rule: round half up, from the exact value, at the stated
8	    number of places. Python's format() rounds binary floats half-even, so
9	    12.5 can print as "12"; here it is always "13".

22	def _exact(x) -> Fraction:
23	    if isinstance(x, bool) or isinstance(x, float):
24	        raise TypeError(f"display takes exact ints or Fractions, never {type(x).__name__}: {x!r}")
25	    if isinstance(x, (int, Fraction)):

31	    f = _exact(x)
32	    with localcontext() as ctx:
33	        ctx.prec = 60
34	        d = Decimal(f.numerator) / Decimal(f.denominator)
35	        q = d.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
36	    s = format(q, "f")
37	    return "0" + s[2:] if s.startswith("-0") and set(s[2:]) <= set("0.") else s

41	    """n/d as a percentage, half up, without a % sign."""
42	    if not isinstance(n, int) or not isinstance(d, int) or isinstance(n, bool) or isinstance(d, bool):
43	        raise TypeError("pct takes integer counts")

46	    if not 0 <= n <= d:

60	    """Cohen's kappa for two binary raters, exactly, from counts: n units, pos_a and pos_b
61	    positives per rater, agree = units where they agree. None when chance agreement is 1."""
62	    for v in (n, pos_a, pos_b, agree):

66	        raise ValueError("kappa needs n > 0")
67	    po = Fraction(agree, n)
68	    pa, pb = Fraction(pos_a, n), Fraction(pos_b, n)
69	    pe = pa * pb + (1 - pa) * (1 - pb)
70	    return None if pe == 1 else (po - pe) / (1 - pe)

107	
108	    def put(self, key: str, text: str, *, source: str, how: str, n: int | None = None, d: int | None = None) -> str:
109	        if key in self.values and self.values[key]["text"] != text:
110	            raise ValueError(f"binding {key} registered twice with different text")
111	        rec = {"text": text, "source": source, "how": how}
112	        if n is not None:
113	            rec["n"] = n
114	        if d is not None:
115	            rec["d"] = d
116	        self.values[key] = rec
117	        return text
118	
119	    def pct(self, key: str, n: int, d: int, places: int, *, source: str, how: str) -> str:
120	        return self.put(key, pct(n, d, places), source=source, how=how, n=n, d=d)
121	
122	    def count(self, key: str, n: int, *, source: str, how: str) -> str:
123	        return self.put(key, count(n), source=source, how=how, n=n)
124	
125	    def texts(self) -> set[str]:
126	        return {v["text"] for v in self.values.values()}
127

129	def selftest() -> None:
130	    cases = [((1, 8, 0), "13"), ((504, 833, 0), "61"), ((1, 2000, 1), "0.1"), ((348, 1645, 1), "21.2"),
131	             ((0, 5, 1), "0.0"), ((5, 5, 0), "100"), ((1, 3, 2), "33.33"), ((2, 3, 0), "67")]
132	    for (n, d, p), want in cases:
133	        got = pct(n, d, p)
134	        assert got == want, (n, d, p, got, want)
135	    for bad in (0.5, True):
136	        try:
137	            round_half_up(bad, 1)
138	        except TypeError:
139	            pass
140	        else:
141	            raise AssertionError(f"accepted {bad!r}")
142	    assert round_half_up(Fraction(-1, 1000), 1) == "0.0"
143	    assert count(17013) == "17,013"
144	    assert ratio(1, 8, 2) == "0.13" and ratio(Fraction(3, 2), 3, 1) == "0.5"
145	    assert kappa(10, 5, 5, 10) == 1 and kappa(4, 4, 4, 4) is None
146	    assert round_half_up(kappa(10, 5, 5, 0), 3) == "-1.000"
147	    assert score(0.12345, 4) == "0.1235" and score(1.0, 2) == "1.00"
148	    for bad in (0.1, Fraction(1, 2)):
149	        try:
150	            cell(bad)
151	        except TypeError:
152	            pass
153	        else:
154	            raise AssertionError(f"cell accepted {bad!r}")

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.11,<3.13"
# dependencies = [
#   "blake3==1.0.11",
#   "duckdb==2.0.0",
#   "matplotlib==3.10.7",
# ]
# ///
"""Negative tests: each display control in build_edition.py must fail on a bad input.

    uv run scripts/test_edition_controls.py

Nothing in the repository is written: templates are temporary files, charts go to
a temporary directory.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
import tempfile
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import build_edition as be  # noqa: E402
import display  # noqa: E402

FAILS: list[str] = []


def expect(name: str, cond: bool) -> None:
    print(("ok    " if cond else "FAIL  ") + name)
    if not cond:
        FAILS.append(name)


def raises(fn, exc) -> bool:
    try:
        fn()
    except exc:
        return True
    return False


def build_with(template: str) -> be.Build:
    b = be.Build("v0.2-draft")
    b.reg.put("as_of", "2026-11-04", source="test", how="test")
    b.reg.put("q_ok", "33,000+", source="test", how="test")
    b.reg.put("n", "137", source="test", how="test")
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".md", delete=False) as f:
        f.write(template)
    old = be.TEMPLATE
    be.TEMPLATE = Path(f.name)
    try:
        b.render("0" * 40)
    finally:
        be.TEMPLATE = old
    return b


FM = "---\nmarp: true\nsize: 16:9\n---\n\n"

# 1-2. exact inputs and one rounding rule
display.selftest()
expect("float input refused", raises(lambda: display.pct(0.5, 1), TypeError))
expect("rounded-column float refused", raises(lambda: display.round_half_up(60.5, 0), TypeError))
expect("half up at a tie (1/8 -> 13)", display.pct(1, 8, 0) == "13")
expect("exact fraction, not the rounded column (504/833 -> 61)", display.pct(504, 833, 0) == "61")
expect("numerator above denominator refused", raises(lambda: display.pct(9, 8), ValueError))
reg = display.Registry()
reg.put("x", "12.2", source="t", how="t")
expect("one binding cannot carry two texts", raises(lambda: reg.put("x", "12.3", source="t", how="t"), ValueError))

# 5. no unbound numerals
b = build_with(FM + "There were 42 firms.\n")
expect("hand-typed numeral in template fails", any("hand-typed numerals ['42']" in e for e in b.errs))
b = build_with(FM + "{{n}} firms in S&P 500 calls, to {{as_of}}.\n")
expect("bound numerals and the S&P 500 name pass", not b.errs)
b = build_with(FM + "Missing {{nope}}.\n")
expect("unresolved binding fails", any("unresolved binding" in e for e in b.errs))
b = be.Build("v0.2-draft")
b.check_text("chart", "peak 0.31%")
expect("unregistered numeral in chart text fails", any("unregistered numerals" in e for e in b.errs))

# 6. quotes
b = build_with(FM + 'They said "a paraphrase".\n')
expect("quoted text that is not a quote binding fails", any("quote binding" in e for e in b.errs))
b = build_with(FM + 'The headline "{{q_ok}}" stands.\n')
expect("quote binding passes", not b.errs)

# 7. clipping and XML
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    be.OUT_DIR = Path(d)
    b = be.Build("v0.2-draft")
    matplotlib, plt = b.mpl()
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3))
    fig.text(0.9, 0.5, "this label runs off the right edge")
    b.save_fig(fig, "clip.svg")
    expect("text past the figure edge fails", any("clipped" in e for e in b.errs))
    expect("malformed SVG fails", raises(lambda: b.save_svg("<svg><text>a & b</text></svg>", "bad.svg"), Exception))

print(f"\n{len(FAILS)} failure(s)")
sys.exit(1 if FAILS else 0)

1	# Adversarial review, 2026-11-04
2	
3	Four independent reviewers read the repository at `a83255b` (branch
4	`ec-ai-corpus`), each from one angle, and tried to break it:
5	
6	1. A stranger rebuilding from a fresh clone.
7	2. Number integrity in the built deck.
8	3. Structure and documentation.
9	4. Method and publication risk.
10	
11	The reviewers were agents. They ran commands in scratch clones and did not
12	touch the working tree. Every finding below gives its evidence. "Ran" means
13	the reviewer confirmed the finding by executing something; "read" means it
14	was found by reading files. The two findings with the largest consequences
15	(H1, H5) were re-checked by hand.
16	
17	Open decisions raised here are in Praxis `OPENQUESTIONS.md`, Q24–Q26.
18	
19	## What holds
20	
21	- **The data layer is sound.**
22	  - `dag.py check` and `status` pass: 36 steps, all `ok`.
23	  - `datasets_md.py check` and `attest_datasets.py verify` pass.
24	  - Ran in a fresh clone.
25	- **The edition build reproduces.** A fresh clone rebuilt all five deck SVGs
26	  byte-identical to the maintainer's copies (ran).
27	- **The edition control tests pass.** `test_edition_controls.py` gives 0
28	  failures in 14 cases (ran).
29	- **Every headline number recomputes exactly.** An independent duckdb
30	  recompute matched all of them (ran):
31	
32	  | Value | Recompute |
33	  |---|---|
34	  | 12.2% of 2026 calls | 214/1760 |
35	  | At most 0.6% before 2023 | 10/1784 |
36	  | 137 firms | 137 |
37	  | Top three risk types by firms | 40, 31, 26 |
38	  | Revenue questions, 21.2% | 348/1645 |
39	  | Controls questions, 0.8% | 13/1645 |
40	  | Executives' safety share, 10% | 18/179 |
41	  | HN 39%, Wikipedia 61%, HN cyber 85% | 2466/6282, 504/833, 2640/3097 |
42	  | CVE credits: Claude, any AI | 370, 924 |
43	
44	  Window boundaries and denominators are correct.
45	- **The Hacker News corpus complies with its own rule.** It stores ids,
46	  offsets and hashes only, with no comment text or usernames (read). The CVE,
47	  Epoch and Wikipedia handling is consistent with their terms (read).
48	- **No secrets, private hostnames or home paths are in tracked files** (read,
49	  pattern scan, values never printed).
50	
51	## High
52	
53	**H1. "137 firms raised AI as a risk" counts analysts' words as the firms'.**
54	`scripts/build_edition.py:237-266` reads `ai-windows.parquet` with no speaker
55	role filter. Counting only company speakers (`issuer_heuristic`) changes the
56	numbers (ran, re-checked):
57	
58	| | All speakers | Company speakers only |
59	|---|---|---|
60	| Firms | 137 | 79 |
61	| Cyber | 40 | 20 |
62	| Safety | 31 | 14 |
63	| Capex | 26 | 14 |
64	
65	The dialogue-space slide separates executives from analysts, so the deck
66	contradicts itself.
67	
68	**H2. The lead chart's rise is mostly growth in AI talk, not a change in
69	framing.** "12.2% of 2026 calls, against at most 0.6% before 2023" is a
70	call-level rate: a call counts if any of its AI windows is flagged. AI windows
71	per call grew from about 1 in 2022 to about 5.7 in 2026. With any constant
72	false-positive rate, the call-level rate rises with volume alone. Per AI
73	window, the v0.1 rate is roughly flat through 2024 (read,
74	`proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/by-year.tsv`):
75	
76	| Fiscal year | Rate per AI window |
77	|---|---|
78	| 2022 | 0.8% |
79	| 2023 | 1.0% |
80	| 2024 | 1.0% |
81	| 2025 | 1.5% |
82	| 2026 | 3.3% |
83	
84	Any real shift shows only in 2025–26, and it is unverified until the gold set
85	is coded. → Q26.
86	
87	**H3. The deck publishes rates its own spec keeps in `proposals/`.**
88	
89	- `docs/bert-enrichment-spec.md` §10 says no count "is citable as a rate of
90	  anything except witness agreement" until precision and recall are measured.
91	- `gold/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/score.tsv`: 0 of 240 rows coded.
92	- The captions state rates as findings; a grey tag on slide 1 does not undo
93	  that.
94	
95	(read) → Q16.
96	
97	**H4. The dialogue-space slide compares levels the spec says are not
98	comparable.**
99	
100	- The spec allows HN-to-call comparison "only in rough order".
101	- The 61% for Wikipedia is partly built in: v0.2's new items were read from
102	  Wikipedia's AI-risk headings and then scored on those same articles.
103	- The executives' cells rest on 179 units.
104	- The three sources use different date windows, hand-typed in
105	  `scripts/v02_map.py:41-50` and not tied to the as-of date. The caption does
106	  not say so.
107	
108	(read)
109	
110	**H5. Verbatim Yahoo-sourced transcript text is redistributed.**
111	
112	- `corpus/earnings-calls/ai-paragraphs.parquet` has a `content` column (28,602
113	  paragraphs with speaker names) (re-checked).
114	- `ai-windows.parquet` has a `text` column (38,600 rows) (re-checked).
115	- `ai-questions.parquet` holds 4,288 full analyst turns.
116	- The only licence is the uploader's ODC-BY tag on Hugging Face. ODC-BY
117	  covers database rights, not copyright in the transcripts. The defeatbeta
118	  card says the data comes from Yahoo Finance and is "intended for research
119	  and educational purposes".
120	- The same text also sits outside the `corpus/` carve-out, so it is implicitly
121	  CC0:
122	  - `proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/risk-quotes-ttm.tsv`
123	  - `oversight-questions.tsv`
124	  - `gold/earnings-calls/*/sample.tsv`
125	- `.zenodo.json` (`cc-zero`) and `CITATION.cff` (`CC0-1.0`) label the whole
126	  deposit CC0.
127	
128	The Hacker News pattern (ids, offsets, hashes, rebuild from the pin) would
129	remove the exposure. → Q24.
130	
131	**H6. A stranger cannot get Praxis.**
132	
133	- `~/dev/praxis` has no git remote.
134	- AGENTS.md names no URL or commit.
135	- The README never says Praxis is needed.
136	
137	Every dataset command in AGENTS.md depends on it (ran). → Q25.
138	
139	**H7. The committed deck is the old hand-built one, and the paper's seal
140	tooling is uncommitted.**
141	
142	- `git show HEAD:DECK.md` cites `scripts/deck_charts.py` (deleted) and
143	  untracked `docs/figures/*.svg`, and mixes two codebooks.
144	- The edition outputs (`deck/STAMP.json` and four SVGs) are untracked, so
145	  `--check` fails at HEAD.
146	- AGENTS.md says to run `scripts/seal.py`, and its README section is missing.
147	  Both exist only in another session's uncommitted work.
148	
149	(ran)

1	# The report as a build product
2	
3	Status, 2026-11-04: the deck is built (`scripts/build_edition.py`); the paper
4	template is not.
5	
6	## Principle
7	
8	The paper is not edited; it is **built**. An edition is a deterministic function
9	of one source commit and a few recorded parameters:
10	
11	    edition = build(source commit, codebook version)
12	
13	Rerunning the build at the same commit with the same parameters gives the same
14	bytes. Building produces a **new commit** whose parent is the source commit, so
15	every edition names exactly the code, data, codebook and prose it came from.
16	
17	`docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md` at `1afb042` ("v0, finalized") is **edition
18	v0**. It was written by hand and stays frozen as it is. Editions from v1 on are
19	built.
20	
21	## What goes in
22	
23	1. **Data**: the steps in `dag.yml`. The build refuses to run unless
24	   `dag.py status` is all `ok`, so every table it reads is locked by hash.
25	2. **One codebook version** for every model-labelled chart and number in the
26	   edition. Mixing versions is a build error. This is the fix for the first
27	   deck, which shows v0.1 charts beside a v0.2-draft chart (executives'
28	   cybersecurity share reads 36% on one slide and 40% on another).
29	3. **Charts**: scripts that turn tables into SVG, with the codebook version
30	   as an argument and printed on the chart.
31	4. **Bindings**: every number in the prose is a reference to a table cell, a
32	   computed value, or a Descartes claim id (`docs/descartes-spec.md`). There
33	   are no hand-typed numbers; a lint fails the build on a bare figure in
34	   bound prose.
35	5. **Prose templates**: the argument, written and reviewed by people
36	   (buzz-saw and brand-voice passes apply to the templates).
37	
38	## What comes out
39	
40	An edition folder holding the rendered paper, the deck, the charts it used,
41	and a stamp file:
42	
43	- source commit;
44	- codebook version;
45	- BLAKE3 of `dag.lock.tsv` (and of the Praxis catalog pin, once the data moves
46	  there);
47	- tool versions (Python packages, Marp CLI);
48	- the BLAKE3 of every output file.
49	
50	A human signs the stamp (the dataset attestation mechanism, applied to the
51	edition). Agents never sign.
52	
53	## Checks the build enforces
54	
55	- every `dag.yml` step `ok`;
56	- one codebook version across all charts and bindings;
57	- every binding resolves; no unbound number in bound prose;
58	- a rebuild at the source commit is byte-identical.
59	
60	## First target
61	
62	`DECK.md` becomes edition output: `deck_charts.py` and the corpus report
63	charts take `--codebook`, slide captions take their numbers from bindings, and
64	the build writes the deck with its stamp. The paper template comes later.
65	
66	## Open decisions
67	
68	Decided 2026-11-04: the build is the review step. It writes the working tree;
69	a person reviews the diff and commits.
70	
71	Everything still open about the report and its PDF is in Praxis
72	`OPENQUESTIONS.md`, Q15–Q23, so it can be discussed in one place: the codebook
73	(Q15), witness rates before a gold set (Q16), where editions live (Q17), what
74	is signed when the PDF does not render reproducibly (Q18), the chart inclusion
75	rule (Q19), outside review (Q20), bindings and Descartes claims (Q21), the data
76	source (Q22) and accessibility (Q23).
77	
78	## Display controls (built, 2026-11-04)
79	
80	Every number that reaches a reader passes through `scripts/display.py`, and the
81	build (`scripts/build_edition.py`) fails on any breach:
82	
83	1. **Exact inputs.** Values are computed from integer counts or exact
84	   fractions. A float raises an error, so a rounded table column can never be
85	   shown, or rounded a second time.
86	2. **One rounding rule.** Half up, from the exact fraction. (Python's own
87	   formatting rounds binary floats half-even, so 12.5 can print as 12.)
88	3. **One source per number.** The build draws every chart in the deck itself,
89	   from the same registered values as the captions.
90	4. **Provenance.** Each value is registered with its source file, computation,
91	   numerator and denominator. `deck/STAMP.json` lists them all.
92	5. **No unbound numerals.** The template may contain no digit outside a
93	   `{{binding}}`. Every numeral in the built deck, and in chart text (axis tick
94	   labels aside), must be a registered value.
95	6. **Quotes.** Quoted text in the template must be a single quote binding, and
96	   each quote must occur verbatim in edition v0.
97	7. **Nothing clipped or malformed.** Chart text must lie inside the figure;
98	   every SVG must parse.
99	8. **One codebook** per edition.
100	
101	`uv run scripts/test_edition_controls.py` feeds each control a bad input and
102	confirms it fails (14 cases).
103	
104	Moving the cross-source chart onto this path changed none of its 125 cell
105	values. The corpus report scripts moved onto `display.py` at `23a4bb6`: no
106	value changed; 113 cells changed format only (fixed decimal places).

221	        R, cb = self.reg, self.cb
222	        scores = ROOT / cb["ec_scores"]
223	        con = duckdb.connect()
224	        as_of = str(con.execute(f"SELECT max(report_date) FROM read_csv('{EC / 'calls.tsv'}')").fetchone()[0])
225	        R.put("as_of", as_of, source="corpus/earnings-calls/calls.tsv", how="max(report_date)")

227	        def flags(h: str) -> str:
228	            return (f"SELECT d.window_id FROM '{scores / 'deberta.parquet'}' d JOIN '{scores / 'modernbert.parquet'}' m "
229	                    f"USING (window_id, hypothesis_id) WHERE d.hypothesis_id = '{h}' "
230	                    f"AND d.p_entail >= {float(THRESHOLD)} AND m.p_entail >= {float(THRESHOLD)}")
231	        cbrows = table(cb["file"])[1]
232	        types = [r["id"] for r in cbrows if r["group"] == "risk_type"]
233	        new = {r["id"] for r in cbrows if r["status"].startswith("v0.2")}
234	        con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE calls AS SELECT symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter, report_date
235	            FROM read_csv('{EC / "calls.tsv"}')
236	            WHERE (duplicate_of IS NULL OR duplicate_of = '') AND n_paragraphs > 2 AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}'""")
237	        con.execute(f"""CREATE TABLE w AS SELECT window_id, symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter,
238	                report_date::DATE AS report_date, regexp_matches(text, '{RISK_WORD}') AS lex,
239	                window_id IN ({flags('ai_risk')}) AS ai_risk
240	            FROM '{EC / "ai-windows.parquet"}'""")
241	        con.execute("""CREATE TABLE cw AS SELECT c.*, bool_or(w.lex) AS lex, bool_or(w.ai_risk) AS nli
242	            FROM calls c LEFT JOIN w USING (symbol, fiscal_year, fiscal_quarter) GROUP BY ALL""")
243	        series = con.execute(f"""SELECT year(report_date)::INT, count(*)::INT,
244	                (count(*) FILTER (WHERE lex))::INT, (count(*) FILTER (WHERE nli))::INT
245	            FROM cw WHERE year(report_date) >= {FIRST_YEAR} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1""").fetchall()
246	        src = f"corpus/earnings-calls/{{calls.tsv,ai-windows.parquet}} + {cb['ec_scores']}"
247	        for y, n, lex, nli in series:
248	            R.pct(f"ec_lex_{y}", lex, n, 1, source=src, how=f"{y}: calls with a 'risk' word in an AI window / calls")
249	            R.pct(f"ec_nli_{y}", nli, n, 1, source=src, how=f"{y}: calls with an ai_risk window (both witnesses) / calls")
250	        last = series[-1]
251	        R.put("ec_year_last", str(last[0]), source=src, how="last calendar year in the series")
252	        R.put("ec_pct_witness_last", R.values[f"ec_nli_{last[0]}"]["text"], source=src, how="= ec_nli_<last year>")
253	        pre = max((r for r in series if r[0] < CUTOFF_YEAR), key=lambda r: Fraction(r[3], r[1]))
254	        R.put("ec_pre2023_max", R.values[f"ec_nli_{pre[0]}"]["text"], source=src,
255	              how=f"max over years < {CUTOFF_YEAR} of ec_nli_<year> (attained {pre[0]})")
256	
257	        since = f"DATE '{as_of}' - INTERVAL {TTM_MONTHS} MONTH"
258	        con.execute(f"CREATE TABLE ttm AS SELECT * FROM w WHERE report_date > {since} AND report_date <= DATE '{as_of}' AND ai_risk")
259	        ranking = []
260	        for t in types:
261	            firms = con.execute(f"SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol)::INT FROM ttm WHERE window_id IN ({flags(t)})").fetchone()[0]
262	            lab = LABELS.get(t, t) + (" *" if t in new else "")
263	            ranking.append((t, lab, firms))
264	            R.count(f"ec_rank_{t}", firms, source=src, how=f"firms with a window both ai_risk and {t}, trailing window")
265	        ranking.sort(key=lambda r: (-r[2], r[0]))
266	        R.count("ec_ttm_risk_firms", con.execute("SELECT count(DISTINCT symbol)::INT FROM ttm").fetchone()[0],
267	                source=src, how="firms with >= 1 ai_risk window, trailing window")
268	        R.put("ec_top3", ", ".join(f"{LABELS.get(r[0], r[0])} ({R.values[f'ec_rank_{r[0]}']['text']})" for r in ranking[:3]),
269	              source=src, how="top three of the ranking")
270	        self.plot_series(series)
271	        self.plot_ranking(ranking)

484	    # ------------------------------------------------------------ deck
485	    def render(self, head: str) -> None:
486	        tpl = TEMPLATE.read_text()
487	        fm_end = tpl.index("\n---\n", 4) + 5
488	        first = tpl[:fm_end].count("\n") + 1
489	        for i, line in enumerate(tpl[fm_end:].splitlines(), first):
490	            bare = re.sub(r"\{\{\w+\}\}", "", re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", "", line))
491	            bare = re.sub(r"!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)", "", bare)   # image directives (w:900) are layout, not data
492	            bad = sorted(tokens(bare) - STATIC_TOKENS)
493	            if bad:
494	                self.errs.append(f"deck.template.md:{i}: hand-typed numerals {bad}")
495	            for q in re.findall(r'"([^"]*)"', re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", line)):
496	                if not re.fullmatch(r"\{\{q_\w+\}\}", q):
497	                    self.errs.append(f"deck.template.md:{i}: quoted text must be one quote binding: \"{q}\"")
498	        self.reg.put("generated_notice", f"<!-- GENERATED by scripts/build_edition.py --codebook {self.codebook} from {head}. "
499	                     "Edit deck/deck.template.md, not this file. -->", source="build", how="notice")
500	        vals = {k: v["text"] for k, v in self.reg.values.items()}
501	        missing = sorted(set(re.findall(r"\{\{(\w+)\}\}", tpl)) - set(vals))
502	        self.errs += [f"unresolved binding {{{{{m}}}}}" for m in missing]
503	        md = re.sub(r"\{\{(\w+)\}\}", lambda m: vals.get(m.group(1), m.group(0)), tpl)
504	        out_body = re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", "", md[md.index("\n---\n", 4) + 5:], flags=re.S)
505	        out_body = re.sub(r"!\[[^\]]*\]\([^)]*\)", "", out_body)
506	        self.check_text("DECK.md", out_body)
507	        self.outs["DECK.md"] = md.encode()
508	
509	    def run(self) -> tuple[dict[str, bytes], list[str]]:
510	        display.selftest()
511	        if not self.preflight():
512	            return {}, self.errs
513	        head = git("rev-parse", "HEAD").strip()
514	        OUT_DIR.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
515	        self.register_static(head)
516	        self.earnings()
517	        self.questions()
518	        self.dialogue()
519	        self.cve()
520	        self.render(head)
521	        stamp = {
522	            "edition_of": head,
523	            "codebook": {"risk": self.codebook, "risk_file": self.cb["file"], "risk_blake3": b3(ROOT / self.cb["file"]),
524	                         "question_intents": QUESTIONS["file"]},
525	            "rule": f"positive = DeBERTa and ModernBERT both >= {self.reg.values['threshold']['text']}",
526	            "rounding": "half up from the exact fraction of integer counts (scripts/display.py)",
527	            "dag_lock_blake3": b3(ROOT / "dag.lock.tsv"),
528	            "paper_v0": f"{PAPER}@{PAPER_V0}",
529	            "tools": {"python": "duckdb==2.0.0 matplotlib==3.10.7 blake3==1.0.11",
530	                      "render": "npx @marp-team/marp-cli@4.1.2 DECK.md --pptx --allow-local-files"},
531	            "values": {k: v for k, v in sorted(self.reg.values.items()) if k != "generated_notice"},
532	            "inputs": {p: b3(ROOT / p) for p in sorted(self.inputs()) if (ROOT / p).is_file()},
533	            "outputs": {k: blake3.blake3(v).hexdigest() for k, v in sorted(self.outs.items())},
534	        }
535	        self.outs["deck/STAMP.json"] = (json.dumps(stamp, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n").encode()
536	        return self.outs, self.errs

539	OUTPUTS = ["DECK.md", "deck/STAMP.json", "deck/ai-risk-by-year.svg", "deck/risk-ranking-ttm.svg",
540	           "deck/intent-ttm.svg", "deck/dialogue-space.svg", "deck/cve-ai-credit.svg"]
541	
542	
543	def main() -> int:
544	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
545	    ap.add_argument("--codebook", required=True, choices=sorted(CODEBOOKS))
546	    ap.add_argument("--check", action="store_true", help="rebuild and compare; leave the tree unchanged")
547	    a = ap.parse_args()
548	    before = {p: (ROOT / p).read_bytes() for p in OUTPUTS if (ROOT / p).exists()}
549	
550	    def restore() -> None:
551	        for p in OUTPUTS:
552	            if p in before:
553	                (ROOT / p).write_bytes(before[p])
554	            elif (ROOT / p).exists():
555	                (ROOT / p).unlink()
556	    outs, errs = Build(a.codebook).run()
557	    if errs:
558	        restore()
559	        print("build failed:\n  " + "\n  ".join(errs), file=sys.stderr)
560	        return 1
561	    if a.check:
562	        diff = sorted(p for p in OUTPUTS if before.get(p) != outs.get(p))
563	        restore()
564	        print("edition is current" if not diff else "edition would change: " + ", ".join(diff))
565	        return 1 if diff else 0
566	    for p, v in outs.items():
567	        (ROOT / p).write_bytes(v)
568	    print(f"built edition of {json.loads(outs['deck/STAMP.json'])['edition_of'][:12]} with risk codebook "
569	          f"{a.codebook}. Review `git diff`, then commit.")
570	    return 0
571	
572	
573	if __name__ == "__main__":
574	    sys.exit(main())

1	"""The one place a number becomes text in a built edition.
2	
3	Rules (docs/report-build.md, "Display controls"):
4	  - Inputs are exact: int counts or fractions.Fraction. A float raises
5	    TypeError, because a float has already been rounded once (binary) and
6	    often twice (a rounded table column). Percentages are computed from counts.
7	  - One rounding rule: round half up, from the exact value, at the stated
8	    number of places. Python's format() rounds binary floats half-even, so
9	    12.5 can print as "12"; here it is always "13".
10	  - Every value shown is registered with its provenance (source file, how it
11	    was computed, numerator and denominator), so the build can prove that every
12	    numeral in the output traces to a registered value.
13	"""
14	
15	from __future__ import annotations
16	
17	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
18	from decimal import ROUND_HALF_UP, Decimal, localcontext
19	from fractions import Fraction
20	
21	
22	def _exact(x) -> Fraction:
23	    if isinstance(x, bool) or isinstance(x, float):
24	        raise TypeError(f"display takes exact ints or Fractions, never {type(x).__name__}: {x!r}")
25	    if isinstance(x, (int, Fraction)):
26	        return Fraction(x)
27	    raise TypeError(f"display takes exact ints or Fractions, not {type(x).__name__}")
28	
29	
30	def round_half_up(x, places: int) -> str:
31	    f = _exact(x)
32	    with localcontext() as ctx:
33	        ctx.prec = 60
34	        d = Decimal(f.numerator) / Decimal(f.denominator)
35	        q = d.quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP)
36	    s = format(q, "f")
37	    return "0" + s[2:] if s.startswith("-0") and set(s[2:]) <= set("0.") else s
38	
39	
40	def pct(n: int, d: int, places: int = 1) -> str:
41	    """n/d as a percentage, half up, without a % sign."""
42	    if not isinstance(n, int) or not isinstance(d, int) or isinstance(n, bool) or isinstance(d, bool):
43	        raise TypeError("pct takes integer counts")
44	    if d <= 0:
45	        raise ValueError(f"pct denominator must be positive, got {d}")
46	    if not 0 <= n <= d:
47	        raise ValueError(f"pct numerator {n} outside 0..{d}")
48	    return round_half_up(Fraction(100 * n, d), places)
49	
50	
51	def ratio(n, d, places: int) -> str:
52	    """n/d as a proportion (0-1 or any exact ratio), half up. n and d are ints or Fractions."""
53	    n, d = _exact(n), _exact(d)
54	    if d == 0:
55	        raise ValueError("ratio denominator is zero")
56	    return round_half_up(n / d, places)
57	
58	
59	def kappa(n: int, pos_a: int, pos_b: int, agree: int) -> Fraction | None:
60	    """Cohen's kappa for two binary raters, exactly, from counts: n units, pos_a and pos_b
61	    positives per rater, agree = units where they agree. None when chance agreement is 1."""
62	    for v in (n, pos_a, pos_b, agree):
63	        if not isinstance(v, int) or isinstance(v, bool):
64	            raise TypeError("kappa takes integer counts")
65	    if n <= 0:
66	        raise ValueError("kappa needs n > 0")
67	    po = Fraction(agree, n)
68	    pa, pb = Fraction(pos_a, n), Fraction(pos_b, n)
69	    pe = pa * pb + (1 - pa) * (1 - pb)
70	    return None if pe == 1 else (po - pe) / (1 - pe)
71	
72	
73	def score(x: float, places: int) -> str:
74	    """A model probability, the one float display accepts. Model scores are measurements,
75	    not counts; they are shown half up from their shortest decimal repr."""
76	    if not isinstance(x, float):
77	        raise TypeError("score takes the model's float probability")
78	    if not 0.0 <= x <= 1.0:
79	        raise ValueError(f"score {x} outside 0..1")
80	    return format(Decimal(repr(x)).quantize(Decimal(1).scaleb(-places), rounding=ROUND_HALF_UP), "f")
81	
82	
83	def cell(v) -> str:
84	    """A table cell. Only ints, strings (already formatted here) and None pass: a float or
85	    Fraction reaching a table means a number skipped the formatting rules."""
86	    if v is None:
87	        return ""
88	    if isinstance(v, bool):
89	        return str(v).lower()
90	    if isinstance(v, int):
91	        return str(v)
92	    if isinstance(v, str):
93	        return v
94	    raise TypeError(f"table cell must be int, str or None, not {type(v).__name__}: {v!r}")
95	
96	
97	def count(n: int) -> str:
98	    if not isinstance(n, int) or isinstance(n, bool):
99	        raise TypeError("count takes an int")
100	    return f"{n:,}"
101	
102	
103	@dataclass
104	class Registry:
105	    """Every displayed value, with where it came from."""
106	    values: dict[str, dict] = field(default_factory=dict)
107	
108	    def put(self, key: str, text: str, *, source: str, how: str, n: int | None = None, d: int | None = None) -> str:
109	        if key in self.values and self.values[key]["text"] != text:
110	            raise ValueError(f"binding {key} registered twice with different text")
111	        rec = {"text": text, "source": source, "how": how}
112	        if n is not None:
113	            rec["n"] = n
114	        if d is not None:
115	            rec["d"] = d
116	        self.values[key] = rec
117	        return text
118	
119	    def pct(self, key: str, n: int, d: int, places: int, *, source: str, how: str) -> str:
120	        return self.put(key, pct(n, d, places), source=source, how=how, n=n, d=d)
121	
122	    def count(self, key: str, n: int, *, source: str, how: str) -> str:
123	        return self.put(key, count(n), source=source, how=how, n=n)
124	
125	    def texts(self) -> set[str]:
126	        return {v["text"] for v in self.values.values()}
127	
128	
129	def selftest() -> None:
130	    cases = [((1, 8, 0), "13"), ((504, 833, 0), "61"), ((1, 2000, 1), "0.1"), ((348, 1645, 1), "21.2"),
131	             ((0, 5, 1), "0.0"), ((5, 5, 0), "100"), ((1, 3, 2), "33.33"), ((2, 3, 0), "67")]
132	    for (n, d, p), want in cases:
133	        got = pct(n, d, p)
134	        assert got == want, (n, d, p, got, want)
135	    for bad in (0.5, True):
136	        try:
137	            round_half_up(bad, 1)
138	        except TypeError:
139	            pass
140	        else:
141	            raise AssertionError(f"accepted {bad!r}")
142	    assert round_half_up(Fraction(-1, 1000), 1) == "0.0"
143	    assert count(17013) == "17,013"
144	    assert ratio(1, 8, 2) == "0.13" and ratio(Fraction(3, 2), 3, 1) == "0.5"
145	    assert kappa(10, 5, 5, 10) == 1 and kappa(4, 4, 4, 4) is None
146	    assert round_half_up(kappa(10, 5, 5, 0), 3) == "-1.000"
147	    assert score(0.12345, 4) == "0.1235" and score(1.0, 2) == "1.00"
148	    for bad in (0.1, Fraction(1, 2)):
149	        try:
150	            cell(bad)
151	        except TypeError:
152	            pass
153	        else:
154	            raise AssertionError(f"cell accepted {bad!r}")

11

13	
14	Nothing in the repository is written: templates are temporary files, charts go to

16	"""
17	
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	import sys
21	import tempfile
22	from fractions import Fraction
23	from pathlib import Path
24	
25	ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
26	sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
27	import build_edition as be  # noqa: E402
28	import display  # noqa: E402
29	
30	FAILS: list[str] = []
31	
32	
33	def expect(name: str, cond: bool) -> None:
34	    print(("ok    " if cond else "FAIL  ") + name)
35	    if not cond:
36	        FAILS.append(name)
37	
38	
39	def raises(fn, exc) -> bool:
40	    try:
41	        fn()
42	    except exc:
43	        return True
44	    return False
45	
46	
47	def build_with(template: str) -> be.Build:
48	    b = be.Build("v0.2-draft")
49	    b.reg.put("as_of", "2026-11-04", source="test", how="test")
50	    b.reg.put("q_ok", "33,000+", source="test", how="test")
51	    b.reg.put("n", "137", source="test", how="test")
52	    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile("w", suffix=".md", delete=False) as f:
53	        f.write(template)
54	    old = be.TEMPLATE
55	    be.TEMPLATE = Path(f.name)
56	    try:
57	        b.render("0" * 40)
58	    finally:
59	        be.TEMPLATE = old
60	    return b
61	
62	
63	FM = "---\nmarp: true\nsize: 16:9\n---\n\n"
64	
65	# 1-2. exact inputs and one rounding rule
66	display.selftest()
67	expect("float input refused", raises(lambda: display.pct(0.5, 1), TypeError))
68	expect("rounded-column float refused", raises(lambda: display.round_half_up(60.5, 0), TypeError))
69	expect("half up at a tie (1/8 -> 13)", display.pct(1, 8, 0) == "13")
70	expect("exact fraction, not the rounded column (504/833 -> 61)", display.pct(504, 833, 0) == "61")
71	expect("numerator above denominator refused", raises(lambda: display.pct(9, 8), ValueError))
72	reg = display.Registry()
73	reg.put("x", "12.2", source="t", how="t")
74	expect("one binding cannot carry two texts", raises(lambda: reg.put("x", "12.3", source="t", how="t"), ValueError))

76	# 5. no unbound numerals
77	b = build_with(FM + "There were 42 firms.\n")
78	expect("hand-typed numeral in template fails", any("hand-typed numerals ['42']" in e for e in b.errs))
79	b = build_with(FM + "{{n}} firms in S&P 500 calls, to {{as_of}}.\n")
80	expect("bound numerals and the S&P 500 name pass", not b.errs)
81	b = build_with(FM + "Missing {{nope}}.\n")
82	expect("unresolved binding fails", any("unresolved binding" in e for e in b.errs))
83	b = be.Build("v0.2-draft")
84	b.check_text("chart", "peak 0.31%")
85	expect("unregistered numeral in chart text fails", any("unregistered numerals" in e for e in b.errs))
86	
87	# 6. quotes
88	b = build_with(FM + 'They said "a paraphrase".\n')
89	expect("quoted text that is not a quote binding fails", any("quote binding" in e for e in b.errs))
90	b = build_with(FM + 'The headline "{{q_ok}}" stands.\n')
91	expect("quote binding passes", not b.errs)
92	
93	# 7. clipping and XML
94	with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
95	    be.OUT_DIR = Path(d)
96	    b = be.Build("v0.2-draft")
97	    matplotlib, plt = b.mpl()
98	    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4, 3))
99	    fig.text(0.9, 0.5, "this label runs off the right edge")
100	    b.save_fig(fig, "clip.svg")
101	    expect("text past the figure edge fails", any("clipped" in e for e in b.errs))
102	    expect("malformed SVG fails", raises(lambda: b.save_svg("<svg><text>a & b</text></svg>", "bad.svg"), Exception))

# Anthropic PBC
-## A counterpoint to the 2026 Public Benefit Report, in charts
+## The public record in charts
-Working paper v0: "released for disagreement, not as a verdict."
-Paper: `docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md`. Every chart here rebuilds from committed files.
+Built from commit `5121b5a465d3` with risk codebook **v0.2-draft** (DRAFT: wording awaits review).
+Every number on these slides is read from a committed table at build time.
-Model output in these charts comes from witnesses: two NLI models whose labels are proposals, not hand-verified findings.
+Model labels come from two NLI witnesses; a label counts only when both score it ≥ 0.5. Labels are proposals, not hand-verified findings: there is no gold set yet.
-## The argument in one line
+## The argument (edition v0 of the paper)
**Anthropic's charter is legally real and legally toothless.**
-- §365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest.
-- §367 limits enforcement to holders of ≥2% (or $2M, lesser, once listed).
+- §365(b) gives directors no duty to any person on account of a public-benefit interest
- The public the charter names cannot enforce it.
-The Report argues from *inputs + intentions* to a discharged public duty. The paper finds that inference unearned (§3).
+Edition v0 of the paper (`docs/anthropic-contrapunctus.md` at `1afb042`) rests on Anthropic's own filings. This deck looks outward at public data.

+
137 firms raised AI as a risk in the 12 months to 2026-11-04. Most named: Cybersecurity (40), Safety / ethics / misuse (31), Overspending / capex return (26).

§1a, Meadows leverage points: Anthropic acts at 12 and 6, declines at 5, 4 and 3, speaks at 2 and 3.

Analysts ask how AI sells (21.2% of AI questions) far more than how its risk is controlled (0.8%). Question-intent codebook v0.1.

Risk–Governance Index v1 on Anthropic's own disclosed risks: 0 of 8 controlled.
-# What the public record shows
-The paper's evidence is Anthropic's own filings. The rest of this deck looks outward at what public data says about AI risk and Anthropic:
-- **S&P 500 earnings calls:** what companies and analysts say about AI.
-- **Hacker News:** what practitioners say about Anthropic and AI security.
-- **Wikipedia:** the map of AI-risk ideas.
-- **The CVE record:** what the vulnerability database credits to AI.
-<!-- _class: chart -->
-![w:900](proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/ai-risk-by-year.svg)

-
AI as a risk on S&P 500 calls: 12.3% of 2026 calls (to 11-04) by both models, up from under 1% before 2023.
-<!-- _class: chart -->
-![h:520](proposals/earnings-calls/codebook-v0.1/report/risk-ranking-ttm.svg)

-

-
Analysts ask how AI sells (21.2% of AI questions) far more than how it is governed (0.8%). This bears on App. E: almost nobody on a call asks about control.
-<!-- _class: chart -->

-
Hacker News discussion of Anthropic is about safety and ethics (40%) far more than executives' calls are (12%). Codebook v0.1; HN precision on safety/ethics is weaker (method doc).

-
The dialogue space, under the DRAFT v0.2 codebook: executives and analysts talk about cyber and capex; Wikipedia covers the field. Draft wording; shares differ from v0.1.

+
Safety and ethics: 10% of executives' AI-risk passages, 39% on Hacker News about Anthropic, 61% on Wikipedia. Cyber dominates HN's AI-security set (85%).
![w:950](deck/cve-ai-credit.svg)

-
The public CVE record credits Claude on 370 CVEs (2020-01 to 2026-10) and any AI system on 924. That cannot confirm or refute "33,000+": not every flaw becomes a CVE, and credits need not name the tool.

## What this deck does not show
- **No effect of Anthropic on any outcome.** Attention and counts only.
-- **No gold set yet.** Every model-labelled chart is a two-witness proposal; precision is unmeasured.

#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = ["duckdb==2.0.0"]
# ///
"""The dialogue space under codebook-v0.2-draft: which sources discuss which AI risks.

For each source, the share of its AI-risk units (both witnesses >= 0.5 on
`ai_risk`) that also carry each risk type (both witnesses >= 0.5). Sources:
  executives   earnings-call windows not spoken by an analyst or the operator, 12 months to 2026-11-04
  analysts     analyst questions on calls, 12 months to 2026-11-04
  hn_anthropic Hacker News Anthropic/Claude windows, 2025-09..2026-08
  hn_security  Hacker News AI-security windows, 2025-09..2026-08
  wikipedia    Wikipedia AI-risk article windows, revisions as of 2026-11-04
DRAFT codebook, witness proposals, no gold set. Writes
proposals/cross-source/codebook-v0.2-draft/report/.

    uv run scripts/v02_map.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import sys
from html import escape
from pathlib import Path

import duckdb

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "scripts"))
import display  # noqa: E402  (the one number-to-text path)
from fractions import Fraction  # noqa: E402
CB = ROOT / "corpus" / "codebooks" / "codebook-v0.2-draft.tsv"
OUT = ROOT / "proposals" / "cross-source" / "codebook-v0.2-draft" / "report"
EC, HN, WP = ROOT / "corpus" / "earnings-calls", ROOT / "corpus" / "hacker-news", ROOT / "corpus" / "wikipedia-ai-risk"
P = ROOT / "proposals"
SOURCES = [  # (key, label, scores dir, id col, unit filter SQL over table u)
    ("executives", "Executives (calls)", P / "earnings-calls/codebook-v0.2-draft", "window_id",
     f"SELECT window_id AS id FROM '{EC / 'ai-windows.parquet'}' WHERE role NOT IN ('analyst_heuristic', 'operator') "
     "AND report_date::DATE > DATE '2025-11-04' AND report_date::DATE <= DATE '2026-11-04'"),
    ("analysts", "Analyst questions", P / "earnings-calls/codebook-v0.2-draft-questions", "question_id",
     f"SELECT question_id AS id FROM '{EC / 'ai-questions.parquet'}' "
     "WHERE report_date::DATE > DATE '2025-11-04' AND report_date::DATE <= DATE '2026-11-04'"),
    ("hn_anthropic", "HN: Anthropic", P / "hacker-news/anthropic-v0.2-draft", "window_id",
     f"""SELECT window_id AS id FROM '{HN / 'windows.parquet'}' WHERE "set" = 'anthropic' AND day BETWEEN '2025-09-01' AND '2026-08-31'"""),
    ("hn_security", "HN: AI security", P / "hacker-news/ai_security-v0.2-draft", "window_id",
     f"""SELECT window_id AS id FROM '{HN / 'windows.parquet'}' WHERE "set" = 'ai_security' AND day BETWEEN '2025-09-01' AND '2026-08-31'"""),
    ("wikipedia", "Wikipedia", P / "wikipedia-ai-risk/codebook-v0.2-draft", "window_id",
     f"SELECT window_id AS id FROM '{WP / 'windows.parquet'}'"),
]


def main() -> int:
    OUT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    cb = list(csv.DictReader(CB.open(), delimiter="\t"))
    types = [r for r in cb if r["group"] == "risk_type"]
    con = duckdb.connect()
    shares: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, int]]] = {}
    for key, _, d, idc, units in SOURCES:
        con.execute(f"""CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE f AS
            SELECT x.{idc} AS id, x.hypothesis_id AS h, x.p_entail >= .5 AND y.p_entail >= .5 AS b
            FROM '{d / 'deberta.parquet'}' x JOIN '{d / 'modernbert.parquet'}' y USING ({idc}, hypothesis_id)
            WHERE x.{idc} IN ({units})""")
